newsitem.title: USA: No Egypt wheat tender yet, traders mixed on timing.
newsitem.headline: No Egypt wheat tender yet, traders mixed on timing.

text.p: U.S. grain exporters said they had received no indications that Egypt would announce a tender for U.S. wheat but most said they did not expect one this week as Egypt's domestic harvest was continuing.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures jumped in morning trade on Wednesday on widespread talk that Egypt would seek up to 750,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, possibly for Sept/Oct shipment.
"I can't confirm anything," said a senior buyer at a major exporter, who added that he doubted Egypt would tender this week, especially in light of the last two days' rally.
CBOT July wheat was up 7-1/2 cents a bushel at $3.24 at 1230 CDT (1730 GMT), 45 minutes ahead of the close.

Officials at the Egyptian embassy in Washington and at the state procurement agency GASC in Cairo declined comment on the rumors. But the head of GASC, Samir el-Shankankiri, said in London on June 19 that his agency had purchased 1.0 million tonnes of Egypt's domestic crop to date, aimed to buy another million tonnes and was in no hurry to return to world markets.
U.S. exporters, however, noted that Egypt normally tenders in mid to late summer.
"They will be in for a couple more cargoes of July and five or six for August," said a second exporter.
A third exporter said a July position would be unlikely, but August or September positions would be likely.
Exporters said Egypt will likely seek U.S. soft red winter wheat because of its low price relative to other classes and origins of wheat.

On Wednesday, U.S. SRW wheat at the Gulf was quoted at around $121.50 FOB for July loading, versus $159 for Australian white wheat. For September loadings, U.S. SRW was being quoted $33 below prices for Australian origin.
The U.S. winter wheat harvest continues in high gear, with talk of excellent yields.
